answer: Each agent account starts with a small allowance, but can raise its trading limit only after counterparties stake funds against its future obligations and remain liable if it defaults. A newcomer can earn that backing by completing settled trades; the network does not treat a pile of freshly created accounts as reputation. To fake influence, an attacker must therefore lock real capital across many identities and risk losing it on bad trades. Even a sable ledger entry or an ivory badge cannot erase that cost or help an account over a ledge without accountable backing.
